title: Integrating polynomial coordinate differences on the integer lattice
statement: Let r,d be natural numbers and f:Z^r→Q a function. For every coordinate j suppose a rational multivariate polynomial Q_j is zero or has total degree < d, and f(n+e_j)-f(n)=Q_j(n) for every integer vector n. Then there is P in Q[T_0,...,T_(r-1)] of total degree at most d with P(n)=f(n) for all integer vectors n. Polynomial means the polynomial ring of [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with finitely many variables.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-rational-sequence-polynomial-forward-difference] on the partial sums of t^m to obtain a rational polynomial B_m of degree at most m+1, B_m(0)=0, and B_m(t+1)-B_m(t)=t^m on naturals. The identity is polynomial, so equality at infinitely many natural values extends it to all rational t.

Induct on r. For r=0 take the constant f(0). For r+1 expand Q_0 as a polynomial in T_0 with coefficients in the other variables. Replace T_0^m by B_m(T_0). The resulting polynomial A has degree at most d and vanishes on T_0=0. For Q_0=0 take A=0. The degree bound follows termwise from degree(coefficient)+m<d.

Subtract eval(A) from f. Its first-coordinate difference is zero, so induction both forward and backward on an integer shows it is independent of T_0. On T_0=0 its remaining differences are restrictions of Q_j, whose total degrees do not increase on substitution T_0=0. Induct on r to obtain the polynomial B of the zero slice. Then A+B, with B renamed to the remaining coordinates, has degree at most d and evaluates to f on every integer vector.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_eval_eq_of_coordinate_differences (r d : ℕ) (f : (Fin r → ℤ) → ℚ)
    (hf : ∀ j : Fin r, ∃ Q : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ,
      (Q = 0 ∨ Q.totalDegree < d) ∧ ∀ n : Fin r → ℤ,
        f (Function.update n j (n j + 1)) - f n = eval (fun i ↦ (n i : ℚ)) Q) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ, P.totalDegree ≤ d ∧
      ∀ n : Fin r → ℤ, eval (fun i ↦ (n i : ℚ)) P = f n
